question.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $x≡35\,(\text{mod}\,11)?$
question.worked_solution:
When we add zero to both sides of a congruence modulo $n$, we can form an equivalent congruence by writing zero as an integer multiple of $n.$ This works because every integer multiple of $n$ is congruent to zero modulo $n.$

In our case, we add zero to both sides of the congruence and then use the fact that  $11\cdot (-3)≡0\,(\text{mod}\,11)$ to rewrite the right-hand side, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+0 & ≡35+0\, & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ x & ≡35+0\, & (\text{mod}\,11) \\  & ≡35+11\cdot (-3)\, & (\text{mod}\,11) \\  & ≡35-33\, & (\text{mod}\,11) \\  & ≡2\, & (\text{mod}\,11)\end{aligned}
$$
